Anomaly

/uh-NOM-uh-lee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anomaly means something that does not fit into the normal order, an irregular or abnormal thing.

The librarian spotted an anomaly in the checkout records: one book appeared to have been returned three days before anyone had ever borrowed it.

Worked Example

Cataloging a hillside of wild poppies, the botanist stopped short at a single blossom growing jet black among thousands of orange ones. She photographed the anomaly from every angle, since nothing in the field's normal pattern could explain it.

One black poppy among thousands of orange ones breaks the field's normal pattern, which is exactly what makes it an anomaly.

How Anomaly Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

irregularity

irregularity: something that breaks an expected pattern or rule

oddity

oddity: a strange or unusual thing

exception

exception: a case that does not follow the general rule

Antonyms

norm

norm: the usual, expected standard

regularity

regularity: the state of following a steady, predictable pattern

How Strong Is It? — quirk → anomaly → freak

quirk vs. anomaly

quirk vs. anomaly: A quirk is a small odd detail that barely disturbs a pattern, while an anomaly is a genuine break from the normal order.

freak vs. anomaly

freak vs. anomaly: An anomaly departs from the expected pattern, but a freak occurrence is so wildly extreme that it seems almost unbelievable.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of anomaly.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-

Prefix — an-: not, without (Greek)

Root — omaly

Root — omaly: from Greek homalos, even or uniform, itself from homos, same

Put it together

Put it together: Anomaly comes from Greek anomalia: the prefix an-, meaning 'not,' attached to homalos, 'even, uniform,' which grew out of homos, 'same.' An anomaly is literally something 'not even with' or 'not the same as' everything around it, the one piece that refuses to match the pattern.

Use the root in a new word: homogenize

Use the root in a new word: homogenize: The dairy homogenizes its milk so that every sip tastes the same, a process named with the Greek root homos, 'same,' the very root hiding inside anomaly.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often academic or technical

Anomaly is common in scientific and statistical writing, as in 'a statistical anomaly' or 'a temperature anomaly,' and it names the irregular thing itself, not the act of deviating. The related adjective anomalous, also taught in this unit, describes something as being an anomaly.
